page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions, AVX-512, and cryptography instructions. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of memory per core.

This server configuration bundles a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included in this instance type, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a distinct performance profile. The server exhibits weak CPU-bound performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression speeds are weak. However, memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 6.2 million operations per second. Conversely, the server achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks, processing 11,784.81 tokens per second for a small 135M model prompt and 2,225.82 tokens per second for a medium 7B model prompt.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 is optimized for workloads that can offload processing to the GPU rather than relying on raw CPU compute. The tradeoff of lower CPU performance makes it less suitable for general-purpose compilation or heavy CPU-bound tasks. It is best suited for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and graphics-accelerated workloads.
